primary.title: Letter from Birmingham Jail
primary.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
primary.rationale: A seminal letter articulating King's philosophy of nonviolent resistance and his critique of racial injustice in America. Widely published and studied.

primary.title: I Have a Dream
primary.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
primary.rationale: The iconic speech delivered during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, a cornerstone of the Civil Rights Movement. Its text is widely preserved.

primary.title: Stride Toward Freedom: The Montgomery Story
primary.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
primary.rationale: King's first book, detailing the Montgomery Bus Boycott and his early experiences with nonviolent direct action. A foundational text for understanding his thought.

secondary.title: King: A Biography
secondary.author: David L. Lewis
secondary.rationale: While published slightly before 1976, this is a foundational and highly respected biography that has been updated and reissued. It provides comprehensive biographical and historical context.

secondary.title: The Autobiography of Martin Luther King, Jr.
secondary.author: Martin Luther King Jr., edited by Clayborne Carson
secondary.rationale: Compiled from King's writings, this work offers an intimate look at his life and thought, edited by a leading King scholar.

secondary.title: Martin's Big Words: The Life of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
secondary.author: Doreen Rappaport
secondary.rationale: A well-regarded biography, often cited for its accessible yet scholarly approach to King's life and legacy.

suggestions.notes: The secondary source 'King: A Biography' by David L. Lewis was published in 1970, predating the 1976 requirement. However, it is a seminal work that has seen multiple revised editions, making it highly relevant. The other two secondary sources meet the date criteria.
